title: Brightest and Best of the Sons of the Morning
description: Brightest and Best of the Sons of the Morning in Tonic Solfa to WESLEY (MASON), doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Reginald Heber wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 108, “Epiphany”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Elevens and Tens (11.10.11.10), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to WESLEY (MASON); any other Elevens and Tens tune fits them as well.
underlay: Bright-est and best of the sons of the morn-ing, Dawn on our dark-ness, and lend us thine aid! Star of the East, the ho-ri-zon a-dorn-ing, Guide where our in-fant Re-deem-er is laid!

lines: Brightest and best of the sons of the morning,
Dawn on our darkness, and lend us thine aid!
Star of the East, the horizon adorning,
Guide where our infant Redeemer is laid!
Say, shall we yield him, in costly devotion,
Odors of Edom, and offerings divine?
Gems of the mountain, and pearls of the ocean,
Myrrh from the forest, or gold from the mine?
Vainly we offer each costly oblation;
Vainly with gifts would his favor secure:
Richer by far is the heart's adoration;
Dearer to God are the prayers of the poor.
Brightest and best of the sons of the morning,
Dawn on our darkness, and lend us thine aid!
Star of the East, the horizon adorning,
Guide where our infant Redeemer is laid.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Reginald Heber died in 1826.
credits: Words by Reginald Heber (1783–1826), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to WESLEY (MASON) by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
